parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify two of the behaviours analysed using total times.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the difference in results between these two behaviours.

text: Mann et al. (lying) analysed some behaviours using total times and some as frequencies.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
What sources of information did Loftus and Pickrell say participants may already have, and
include in their false memory?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
How did Loftus and Pickrell explain the inclusion of this information into the memory of the
false event?

text: Loftus and Pickrell suggested that a false memory may ‘evolve’ from fragments of memory, that is,
from other information.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: What did they hope would change about the distribution of scores?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: In what way was the revised test better at detecting differences than the original test?

text: Baron-Cohen et al. hoped that the revised eyes test would be better at detecting differences than
the original eyes test.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the different movements made by the active kitten that the carousel reproduced for
the passive kitten.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the difference in experience between the active and passive kittens.

text: In the study by Held and Hein, a piece of apparatus called the ‘kitten carousel’ was used.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what the participant saw when they pressed a switch on the shock generator.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why these events were important to the study.

text: In the study by Milgram (obedience) a ‘shock generator’ was used.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Who did the researchers ask about the design of the prison?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why a realistic simulation of a prison was important to the study.

text: In their study, Haney, Banks and Zimbardo used various sources of information to design the
prison simulation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the critical area of the subway car.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State how many people left the critical area and explain why they might have done so.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what is meant by validity.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one reason why this study is valid.

text: Tajfel studied intergroup categorisation:

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why the children’s pre-existing levels of aggression were rated.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The aggression scores given to each participant by the two observers were correlated.
Explain why this was done.

text: In the study by Bandura et al., some of the participants were initially rated for aggression by two
independent observers.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what this belief led little Hans to expect.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Outline and explain one dream or fantasy relating to little Hans’s widdler.

text: Freud reported that little Hans believed all animate objects (living things) had a ‘widdler’ (penis)
like he did but that inanimate (non-living) ones did not.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Name and describe one ethical guideline.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain how this ethical guideline was followed in this study.

text: Demattè et al. studied smells and facial attractiveness.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why the pseudo-patients were nervous on admission to the hospitals.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest why the nervousness of the pseudo-patients might have been important to the study.

text: From the study by Rosenhan (sane in insane places):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: What were the results of the IQ tests for the two personalities?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain, for one personality, why her score may have been lower than her actual IQ.

text: In the study by Thigpen and Cleckley (multiple personality disorder), IQ tests were conducted.

parts.text:
Describe the sex ratios of the student participants who were studying physical sciences and
humanities.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest how you could increase the performance of girls on system-related tasks.

parts.text: Describe how data were gathered about long mirror sessions.

parts.text:
In the questionnaire for short sessions, the participants were not asked about distress after
resisting mirror gazing. Explain why this omission was important.
